existing_implementations.representation: Mean residual at the explicitly named concept token across 20 templates, minus the mean across concepts.
Same mean-difference probe; task subjects preselected for GPT-2 XL.
J-token, logit-token and random directions; no learned-probe arm.

findings: All 20 templates explicitly name the concept; they are lexical contexts, not evidence that the concept is represented implicitly.
Only the causal prefix through the concept can affect its activation. Suffix-only template variants must not cross train/test splits.
The local templates are reusable training contexts, not Anthropic's implied-intermediate probe training prompts.
No exact template-filled prompt overlaps the task prompts. This lexical non-overlap is weaker than semantic independence.
Task answers and swap outcomes are not probe-training labels. Classes are concept names.
The Qwen notebook records single-token flags but its correct_trials filter does not enforce them; first-token concept fallbacks can enter its swaps.
The legacy claim that vector scale does not matter is too broad: a common scale cancels, but different source and target rescalings change the swap.

new_protocol.readout: Last token of the complete concept mention, located with character offsets and checked against model encoding.
cohorts: matched single-token concepts: learned probes, J, logit and matched random controls
additional multi-token concepts: learned probes and their matched random controls only
limitations: Held-out-template accuracy measures explicitly named concepts, not latent semantic decoding.
Classifier directions are readout covectors used experimentally as write directions; classification accuracy does not establish causal usefulness.
This is not the paper's sparse J-space/remainder decomposition experiment.
Direction norms are preserved; each learned arm has a separate random control matched to its actual per-layer, per-position perturbation norm.
